routes.approach: Follow the Whitney Trail from Whitney Portal up to Trail Crest, a long climb that many parties split with a night at Trail Camp, the highest dependable water. From the crest, walk north down the trail a short distance, stopping before the junction with the John Muir Trail, then scramble steeply east up loose scree and blocks until you reach the rim. routes.name: SouthWest Edge
routes.approach: Take the Whitney Trail, from Whitney Portal past Trail Crest and north along the base of the summit mass, to the saddle that separates Whitney from Keeler Needle, which the trail passes close by. The climb starts in that saddle. A Whitney Zone permit from Inyo National Forest is required: a day-use permit for a car-to-car push, or the Whitney Trail overnight permit if you camp.

routes.name: SouthWest Ridge
routes.approach: Take the Whitney Trail, from Whitney Portal past Trail Crest and north along the base of the summit mass, to the saddle that separates Whitney from Keeler Needle, beside the trail. Leave the trail there and head northeast up to the summit area. A Whitney Zone permit from Inyo National Forest is required: a day-use permit for a car-to-car push, or the Whitney Trail overnight permit if you camp.
routes.descent: The scramble ends on the flat summit area. Walk down the Whitney Trail, marked by cairns, back past the notch where the scramble started; the trail leads south to Trail Crest and then east down to Whitney Portal.
